overall.label: Yellow
overall.headline: AI selloff drags stocks 8% below their record
overall.text: The S&P fell six days in a row, led by chip stocks, after Nvidia's CEO quit. The Fed looks set to hike in December. Oil fell to about $92. Junk-bond spreads widened, but are still well short of stress.

powder.label: Build — steady
powder.action: Keep new contributions going to Bond Plus. Make no transfers yet; the S&P fund is 8.2% below its high, about 2% above the 10% deploy zone (~7,037).
powder.note: If the S&P closes below ~7,037 while junk spreads stay under ~400bp, the call moves to Deploy. Cash earns about 4.2%, only ~0.5 pts above the last full-year inflation read (3.7%). Not financial advice.

regime.label: Choppy
regime.text: A bumpy month: two sharp AI-chip selloffs and a 7.5% slide, but credit barely moved. It brings stocks closer to the buy zone without changing the longer-trend call yet.

ranges.label: 10-yr yield
ranges.note: Dipped to 4.84% in Nov 5 selloff, then rebounded

ranges.label: VIX (fear)
ranges.note: Peaked at month's end; never closed above 30

ranges.label: Junk spreads
ranges.note: Peak only 15bp above start; far from 400bp stress

ranges.label: Brent oil
ranges.note: Fell ~$26 from Oct 30 high as Hormuz traffic recovered

events.text: AI-chip selloff: S&P −4.4%, worst day since 2025; VIX jumped to 28.2.
Trump signals restraint on Iran; Brent −5.9% to $92.57 and S&P +2.3%.
October CPI +0.4%, above forecast; markets now see a December Fed hike as near-certain.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns; Nvidia −4.3% and 10-yr yield rises to 5.11%.
Anthropic IPO jumps 17% on debut, yet S&P falls 2.0%, its sixth straight loss.

interim.basis: Built from 19 logged trading days plus Nov 13–19 values filled from sourced news and FRED (log ends Nov 13). Calm/Choppy/Turbulent = worst of VIX peak, biggest S&P dip, junk-spread widening.

outlook.text: The Dec 8–9 Fed meeting and AI-stock nerves dominate. A drop into the 10% deploy zone is quite possible.
Strong profits are fighting Fed hikes and 5% yields. Expect a range, with a good chance to buy lower.
Earnings grew over 30% this year and stocks got cheaper. A year out, prices should be higher if profits hold.

consensus.note: Goldman and Morgan Stanley say buy stocks for 2027. BlackRock, PIMCO and Schwab lean toward high-quality bonds at today's yields.

houses.change: Raised global stocks to 'maximum overweight', its most bullish stance, saying risk assets cheapened.
houses.fitNote: Argues for adding to the S&P fund now rather than building more cash in Bond Plus.

houses.change: Rolled its target forward from 8,000 for end-2026 to 8,700 for end-2027.
houses.fitNote: An 18% expected return would favor the S&P fund over Bond Plus's yield.

houses.change: Turned more positive on bonds for the first time since 2020, citing the risk that AI spending slows.
houses.fitNote: Neutral stocks plus warmer bonds fits sending contributions to Bond Plus.

houses.change: Warned many portfolios have drifted too heavily into stocks and favored bonds at high real yields.
houses.fitNote: Backs holding dry powder in Bond Plus while yields are high.

houses.equities: Cautious; lower P/E isn't a bottom
houses.change: Turned more hawkish after hot CPI, asking not whether the Fed hikes in December but by how much.
houses.fitNote: Bond yields near 20-year highs support adding to Bond Plus for now.

voices.context: At the October press conference, where the Fed held rates but flagged rising energy prices.

voices.quote: If you really want to get it down you've got to start taking aggressive actions.
voices.context: Making the case for a half-point hike at the Dec 8–9 meeting.

street.note: These views are context, not a vote. Wall Street is often wrong together, and these views never change the dry-powder call on their own.

macro.name: AI & tech stocks
macro.note: Nasdaq 100 fell about 10% in a month as Nvidia's CEO quit and new China chip curbs hit.

macro.name: Inflation & Fed
macro.note: October CPI rose 0.4% (core 0.3%), above forecast; a December hike is ~95% priced.

macro.name: Oil & Middle East
macro.note: Brent fell to ~$92 as Hormuz traffic recovered, though Iran's mines still hit tankers.

macro.name: Labor market
macro.note: October added 165K jobs and unemployment fell to 4.1%; no recession signal.

macro.name: Credit
macro.note: Junk spreads rose to 347bp and CCC to 1,353bp; weakest borrowers strain, but no crisis.

macro.name: Crypto sentiment
macro.note: Bitcoin near $62K, about half its 2025 peak, shows speculative appetite is fading fast.

pullback.note: The S&P is 8.2% below its Oct 6 record. The deploy zone starts at a 10% pullback (~7,037); a 20% pullback (~6,255) is a major opportunity.

board.change: Up from +29%; forward EPS +3.3% since Sep 30
+0.08 pts; cash beats inflation by ~0.5 pts
Above forecast; no yearly rate due to 2025 shutdown gap
Up from ~89%; some talk of 0.50 pts

red: Fed hikes 0.50 pts and signals more; 10-yr above 5.5%
Unemployment at 4.5%+ or Sahm rule near 0.5
green: S&P closes below ~7,037 (−10%) with junk spreads under 400bp
Fed signals hikes are done; 10-yr falls below ~4.75%

swans: AI unwind: chip selloff spreads into AI debt and credit markets
Wider Gulf war: Hormuz mines and strikes cut oil flows again
Fed over-tightens: half-point hikes push the 10-yr toward 6%
